entries.reason: the port composes the release's own -setValue:forPasteboardType: over the release's own type lists
entries.effect: each object is stored through the release's own -setValue:forPasteboardType:, under the first entry of the release's own type list for its class - the string list for a string or for anything describable, the URL list for an NSURL. The first entry because the port answers only for the type it was given: storing under every entry would write the same bytes under type strings the application did not ask about, and -dataForPasteboardType: would answer for types it never named - so if a list holds one entry the first is the only choice, and if it holds several the rest are left as the release has them. An object with no description, or a release naming no list, is not stored, because the release would have no type to store it under. How many entries each list holds is measured by tests/backports/device/pasteboard10.m, which prints the count beside the provenance check
entries.source: objc.inventory on the 6.1.3 and 4.3 caches, whose negative controls both answered 'the port must carry it', says the release ships UIPasteboard with -setItems:, -items and -setValue:forPasteboardType:, and the release's selector table holds all three; the type lists are the release's own, read the same way in facts/UIKit/UIPasteboardIOS10.md
